messages.subject: rstan 2.8.1 released
messages.body_plain:
> A new version of rstan was released on CRAN last week and by now binaries are available for Windows and any Mac OS since Mavericks. I, however, forgot to commit the NEWS file, so there is no indication as to what changed. Since StanHeaders was not updated, there are no changes in what Stan can do, only changes in the R code surrounding it. There were some bugs that were fixed, although a couple more were apparently introduced and already discovered:
> Passing arguments through the ... of stan() will not work directly because they get passed to stanc() accidentally. This includes chain_id, init_r, test_grad, refresh, and enable_random_init. To work around this, you can first call stan_model() and then pass that to sampling() along with init_r, refresh, etc. Or you can install rstan from github
> devtools::install_github("stan-dev/rstan", ref = "v2.8.1-1", subdir = "rstan/rstan")
> Calling expose_stan_functions() on a .stan file with print() statements in user-defined Stan functions will not work at the moment. You can comment out the print() statements or shortly call
> source("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stan-dev/rstan/develop/rstan/rstan/R/expose_stan_functions.R") # R >= 3.2.2 or
> devtools::source_url("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stan-dev/rstan/develop/rstan/rstan/R/expose_stan_functions.R")
>
> The main goal of rstan 2.8.1 was to get ready for the release of the rstanarm package, which has been basically usable for a couple months but is not on CRAN yet because a few things are still missing. If you have rstan >= 2.8.1 installed already, you can install rstanarm for testing via
> devtools::install_github("stan-dev/rstanarm", local = FALSE)
> For those of you that do not already know, rstanarm is a package that has several Stan programs that are compiled at (or before) installation time, a few R functions that call these Stan programs using the conventional "formula, data, other_arguments" R syntax, and a bunch of R functions that analyze and / or plot the results.
>
> To get rstanarm onto CRAN (in the near future) we had to overcome the problem that Kevin, Sebastian, and others have asked about how to write an R package that comes with Stan models and works on all platforms (including 32 bit Windows). The rstan 2.8.1 package has two functions that make this much easier, whereas it was pretty much impossible with rstan <= 2.8.0.
> The stanc_builder() function is a lot like stanc() --- which you may or may not have ever called directly but is what parses a Stan program and outputs the corresponding C++ --- but has two differences.
> The obfuscate_model_name argument defaults to FALSE (whereas it defaults to TRUE in stanc). This means that the C++ class defining the model has a predictable name rather than a randomly-generated one (which prevents name clashes in conventional rstan use).
> The stanc_builder() function --- unlike stanc() --- reads a .stan file into R, replaces lines that have C++ style #include statements with the included files, and writes the amalgamated .stan file to the tempdir() before parsing and compiling it. For example, you can have something like
> functions {
>   #include "common_functions.txt"
> }
> and stanc_builder will find the file called "common_functions.txt" (looking in the same directory as the .stan file by default but there is an isystem argument that can be specified as a different directory to look in) and put it where #include "common_functions.txt" appears to yield something like
> functions {
>   vector sqrt_vector(vector x) {
>     vector[rows(x)] out;
>     for (i in 1:rows(x)) out[i] <- sqrt(x[i]);
>     return out;
>   }
> }
> if common_functions.txt consisted solely of that sqrt_vector function. These C++-style include statements can be used anywhere in a Stan program but are not chainable (i.e. common_functions.txt cannot #include "helpers.txt"; you have to #include "helpers.txt" in your Stan program first and then #include "common_functions.txt" second). Basically, this makes it possible to maintain an informal library of Stan functions and code snippets that can be reused in multiple Stan programs without having to copy-and-paste a bunch of duplicated code. The rstanarm package uses this mechanism extensively. Right now, we have 1170 lines of code spread over six .stan files and 388 lines of code spread over 13 .txt files that are #included into many of those six .stan files.
> The rstan.package.skeleton() function works a lot like base R's package.skeleton() function and Rcpp's rcpp.package.skeleton() function in that it will create a directory that has an outline of what is needed to create a R package of Stan programs that are driven by rstan (which is put under Imports in the DESCRIPTION file). The rstan.package.skeleton() function downloads some GPLv3 code from the rstanarm GitHub repository to make this work, so either be comfortable with licensing your R package under the GPLv3, or don't distribute your R package outside your company, or don't use these downloaded files. Basically a package like rstanarm has the following minimal structure:
> -rwxr-xr-x 1 goodrich goodrich  287 Oct 18 14:49 cleanup       # downloaded from rstanarm
> -rwxr-xr-x 1 goodrich goodrich  287 Oct 18 14:49 cleanup.win   # downloaded from rstanarm
> -rw-r--r-- 1 goodrich goodrich 1433 Nov 18 00:06 DESCRIPTION   # created by rstan.package.skeleton
> drwxr-xr-x 2 goodrich goodrich 4096 Oct 31 16:26 exec          # a subdirectory for Stan programs and #included .txt files
> drwxr-xr-x 2 goodrich goodrich 4096 Nov 23 01:35 man           # you need to fill this in, as usual for an R package
> -rw-r--r-- 1 goodrich goodrich 3241 Nov 23 01:35 NAMESPACE     # you need to fill this in, as usual for an R package
> drwxr-xr-x 2 goodrich goodrich 4096 Nov 20 17:16 R             # some code downloaded from rstanarm; fill in the rest
> -rw-r--r-- 1 goodrich goodrich  211 Nov  1 13:54 .Rbuildignore # downloaded from rstanarm
> drwxr-xr-x 3 goodrich goodrich 4096 Nov 23 00:53 src           # a few files are autogenerated by rstan.package.skeleton
> drwxr-xr-x 2 goodrich goodrich 4096 Oct 31 11:28 tools         # downloaded from rstanarm
> The cleanup and cleanup.win bash files are called when you do R CMD build or R CMD INSTALL --preclean but in this case, they ironically create C++ files in the src/ directory by executing an R helper file in tools/, which looks for files with a .stan extension under exec/, parses them with stanc_builder(), and glues all the C++ together under src/ (otherwise you will get linker errors that we have not figured out yet). At that point, R CMD INSTALL including R CMD INSTALL --build will work "as usual" for an R package that has Rcpp-style C++ files, which is to say both the 64bit and 32bit shared objects will be built under libs/ unless --no-multiarch is passed. This is the only mechanism that is currently known to work for packages with pre-built Stan programs and many other mechanisms are known to not work in some respect. So, if you want to create a package like rstanarm that comes with pre-built Stan programs, this is the best way to go. Inside the package's namespace, there will be a named list of objects of stanmodel class (with corresponding entries under the RcppModules line in DESCRIPTION) that are essentially equivalent to what you could get if you called stan_model("foo.stan"). In particular, your package's R functions can pass them to rstan::sampling() or rstan::optimizing(). You may also want to put rstanarm in Imports or Suggests and utilize the generic functions we have written for analyzing the results. Or consider making a pull request on GitHub to have your code incorporated into rstanarm. But if you decide to maintain an R package yourself, it is best to follow rstanarm's wake. Otherwise, it will be more difficult for us to upload new versions of rstan without breaking the R packages that depend on it.
>
> Ben
>

> There were some bugs that were fixed, although a couple more were apparently introduced and already discovered:
> Passing arguments through the ... of stan() will not work directly because they get passed to stanc() accidentally. This includes chain_id, init_r, test_grad, refresh, and enable_random_init. To work around this, you can first call stan_model() and then pass that to sampling() along with init_r, refresh, etc. Or you can install rstan from github
> devtools::install_github("stan-dev/rstan", ref = "v2.8.1-1", subdir = "rstan/rstan")
> Calling expose_stan_functions() on a .stan file with print() statements in user-defined Stan functions will not work at the moment. You can comment out the print() statements or shortly call
> source("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stan-dev/rstan/develop/rstan/rstan/R/expose_stan_functions.R") # R >= 3.2.2 or

These were fixed in RStan 2.8.2, which is available in binary form from CRAN mirrors now.

Ben
